proofs.heading: In one sentence
proofs.requirement: A tumor-informed molecular residual disease assay uses features identified in a tumor sample to look for a qualifying tumor signal in later blood samples.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: A tumor-informed molecular residual disease assay uses features identified in a tumor sample to look for a qualifying tumor signal in later blood samples.

semanticAssessment.explanation: Sampled-tumour selected features and predefined detector rules are explicit, with initial tumour/reference inputs separated from later plasma. Matched normal addresses origin and does not become a universal requirement.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A tumour-informed test uses a sampled tumour reference to select features for later tracking in plasma. The reference can come from a suitable biopsy or resection; it is not necessarily a surgically removed whole tumour or a complete inventory of tumour clones. Reference quality, selected targets, plasma input, background and the calling rule affect performance. A fixed list can miss features outside it, including variants that emerge after the reference was sampled.

A tumour-naive or tumour-agnostic method uses predefined features without first building that person's tumour reference. It still needs suitable input and a validated detector, and it does not promise a complete mutation profile. FDA's November 2024 drug-development guidance describes strengths and limits of both approaches rather than a universal ranking. Santonja's same-sample breast-cancer comparison supports its particular assays at low signal, not every branded product. Magbanua's 2025 study also found retained assay variants in sampled resistant tumours from some patients with negative plasma; a negative draw does not by itself prove that the reference targets disappeared.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Design contract, from the FDA guidance of November 2024: a tumour-informed approach sequences the tumour and selects variants to follow. Its stated advantage is potentially higher specificity, and its limits include lag between tumour testing and panel creation, possible failure to detect mutations that emerge after tumour sampling or revert, and dependence on the number and reliability of selected targets, which may be better for tumours with higher mutation burden and well-characterised hotspot variants. A tumour-naive or tumour-agnostic panel is generic, with faster turnaround as its stated advantage and tumour biomarkers outside the panel as a limit. Both still meet the same finite plasma tube, background attribution and calling rules.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The reference and plasma workflows both have acceptance rules. Tumour material can be insufficient or unrepresentative, tracked features can be lost or absent from another clone, and plasma can have low signal, poor recovery or background. Keep the initial tissue and matched-normal requirements separate from the later consumed plasma aliquot. FDA's November 2024 guidance asks for evaluation of the complete workflow, actual panel designs, representative clinical specimens, input ranges and sampling schedules; personalisation alone does not validate a clinical decision.

proofs.heading: The intuition
proofs.requirement: The analogy holds for sensitivity as a general pattern: knowing exactly what to look for usually lets an assay find fainter traces. It breaks for coverage. A fingerprint taken from one biopsy cannot match a clone that was not in that biopsy, and it cannot exist until the tumor has been sequenced.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: The analogy holds for sensitivity as a general pattern: knowing exactly what to look for usually lets an assay find fainter traces. It breaks for coverage. A fingerprint taken from one biopsy cannot match a clone that was not in that biopsy, and it cannot exist until the tumor has been sequenced.

semanticAssessment.explanation: Use-specific design considerations replace a universal category ranking. A fixed feature list can miss an unrepresented feature; absence of a clone from the biopsy does not necessarily make all its shared features untrackable. Neither predefined nor personalised design guarantees new-variant discovery. The patrol/fingerprint analogy is retained only at this qualified feature-scope level.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Choosing a reference strategy is a fit question. Available tumour tissue and very low expected signal can favour tracking many known tumour features, as in the same-sample Santonja comparison. A predefined assay can begin without building a patient-specific tumour reference, which may matter when tissue is unavailable or time is limited. Looking for newly emerged resistance variants requires coverage of those variants: a broader predefined panel may include them, but neither category detects features outside its measured scope. These are design considerations rather than a general ranking of sensitivity or clinical benefit.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Separate three test jobs. Tumour-informed monitoring asks whether selected known tumour features reached the plasma sample; it need not discover new variants outside that list. Reference-free monitoring asks whether a qualifying cancer-associated signal is present without prior tumour sequencing; it need not return a complete genomic profile. Plasma genomic profiling asks which covered alterations are detectable; it does not automatically have a dedicated low-signal monitoring assay's sensitivity. Real methods can combine features. Methylation and fragment-pattern analysis need not produce a mutation list, and a captured circulating tumour cell is a cell, a different object from cell-free DNA fragments.

proofs.heading: How it works
proofs.requirement: For [molecular residual disease (MRD)](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/liquid-biopsy/mrd) monitoring with [circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA)](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/liquid-biopsy/cfdna-vs-ctdna), a tumor-informed mutation assay sequences tumor material to select features for later tracking in plasma. Matched normal material may help distinguish [inherited from tumor-acquired variants](/wiki/education/concepts/biology-basics/genetics/germline-vs-somatic) and blood-cell-derived signals. The assay's design determines how many features are tracked and what combination qualifies as positive.

proofs.heading: How it works
proofs.requirement: A **tumor-naive** assay does not require a patient-specific tumor reference to construct its detector. It may examine a fixed variant panel, [methylation or fragment features](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/liquid-biopsy/fragmentomics-and-methylation), or combinations. “Tumor-naive,” “tumor-agnostic” and “tissue-free” are method labels that need definition: they do not establish that a test detects every cancer or never uses clinical context.

proofs.heading: How it works
proofs.requirement: An assay sees only the genome copies put into it (see [limit of detection and sampling](/wiki/education/concepts/measurement/liquid-biopsy/limit-of-detection-and-sampling)). In the breast-cancer study below, a standard input was 4,500 genome copies of cell-free DNA (cfDNA), about 15 nanograms. At a tumor fraction of 1 in 100,000, any single tumor position is then usually absent by chance. Each additional tumor-specific variant is another, largely independent chance to catch a tumor fragment. The study's theoretical detection limit was 1 ÷ (input copies × variants tracked): with 4,500 copies and 47 variants, 1 in 211,500, or 4.7 parts per million. Knowing the exact variants also lets the assay ignore everything else, which lowers background error. Whole-genome designs push the same logic further, integrating thousands of tumor mutations to reach tumor fractions near 1 in 100,000 ([Zviran 2020](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41591-020-0915-3)).

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

Whole-genome sequencing of cfDNA integrates thousands of mutations and reached tumour-fraction sensitivity as low as 10 to the minus 5 (Zviran 2020).

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) can be reported as a concentration, as a fraction, or as a yes or no call, and the three are not interchangeable. A concentration counts tumour-attributed molecules in a stated volume of plasma. One example is mean tumour molecules per millilitre (MTM/mL), which the I-SPY 2 breast-cancer study of Magbanua and colleagues used for ctDNA across tracked variants. A fraction divides tumour-attributed molecules by a stated total, such as all evaluated alleles at one position (variant allele fraction, VAF) or all evaluated DNA (an estimated tumour fraction). Parts per million (PPM) is a fraction multiplied by one million, so the number is only as meaningful as the fraction it scales: 0.01% is 100 PPM, and 0.00024% is 2.4 PPM, the lowest allele fraction Santonja and colleagues reported for ctDNA detection in breast cancer.

Concentration and fraction can move apart. If two equal one-millilitre aliquots each hold the same number of tumour molecules but one holds more background cell-free DNA, the concentration is unchanged and the fraction falls. A detection call and a reliable amount are also different claims, because the detection limit and the quantitation range are validated separately. Nothing here gives a conversion between assays: MTM/mL cannot be turned into PPM from the printed result, and a VAF of 100 PPM at one variant is not a tumour fraction of 100 PPM.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
A tumour-informed test uses a sampled tumour reference to select features for later tracking in plasma. The reference can come from a suitable biopsy or resection; it is not necessarily a surgically removed whole tumour or a complete inventory of tumour clones. Reference quality, selected targets, plasma input, background and the calling rule affect performance. A fixed list can miss features outside it, including variants that emerge after the reference was sampled.

A tumour-naive or tumour-agnostic method uses predefined features without first building that person's tumour reference. It still needs suitable input and a validated detector, and it does not promise a complete mutation profile. FDA's November 2024 drug-development guidance describes strengths and limits of both approaches rather than a universal ranking. Santonja's same-sample breast-cancer comparison supports its particular assays at low signal, not every branded product. Magbanua's 2025 study also found retained assay variants in sampled resistant tumours from some patients with negative plasma; a negative draw does not by itself prove that the reference targets disappeared.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) can be reported as a concentration, as a fraction, or as a yes or no call, and the three are not interchangeable. A concentration counts tumour-attributed molecules in a stated volume of plasma. One example is mean tumour molecules per millilitre (MTM/mL), which the I-SPY 2 breast-cancer study of Magbanua and colleagues used for ctDNA across tracked variants. A fraction divides tumour-attributed molecules by a stated total, such as all evaluated alleles at one position (variant allele fraction, VAF) or all evaluated DNA (an estimated tumour fraction). Parts per million (PPM) is a fraction multiplied by one million, so the number is only as meaningful as the fraction it scales: 0.01% is 100 PPM, and 0.00024% is 2.4 PPM, the lowest allele fraction Santonja and colleagues reported for ctDNA detection in breast cancer.

Concentration and fraction can move apart. If two equal one-millilitre aliquots each hold the same number of tumour molecules but one holds more background cell-free DNA, the concentration is unchanged and the fraction falls. A detection call and a reliable amount are also different claims, because the detection limit and the quantitation range are validated separately. Nothing here gives a conversion between assays: MTM/mL cannot be turned into PPM from the printed result, and a VAF of 100 PPM at one variant is not a tumour fraction of 100 PPM.

proofs.requirement: - “Personalized” does not mean a clinical decision has been individually validated.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: - “Personalized” does not mean a clinical decision has been individually validated.

semanticAssessment.explanation: Personalisation, blood-cell attribution and finite-sampling uncertainty are distinct. A reference cannot create absent molecules or independently validate a clinical decision.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional workflow, method A must select a fixed variant list from suitable tumour DNA before testing later plasma, while method B already has a predefined validated detector. If tumour DNA is unavailable but qualifying plasma is available, B can start as specified and A cannot build its reference yet. Reference-build failure is not a negative plasma result. Neither fixed list establishes detection outside its features, and a tumour reference and a blood-cell-origin filter address different questions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional model, an evaluated aliquot supplies 4,500 independent amplifiable opportunities at one locus, each with a target-allele probability of 1 in 10,000. The expected target count is 0.45. If target counts follow a Poisson distribution, the chance of no target is exp(-0.45), 63.8%. Twenty independent loci with the same opportunity count and probability give an expected total of 9 and exp(-9), 0.012%, for none. Independence, equal recovery and one retained target being sufficient are assumptions of this model. These are not measured clinical false-negative rates. A tumour-DNA fraction cannot simply replace the target-allele probability without assumptions about copy number, variant multiplicity and which tumour clones carry the variant. More reads cannot recover an original molecule absent from the aliquot.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Choosing a reference strategy is a fit question. Available tumour tissue and very low expected signal can favour tracking many known tumour features, as in the same-sample Santonja comparison. These are design considerations rather than a general ranking of sensitivity or clinical benefit.

proofs.requirement: **A large pile of recycling material can mean fast collection or failed clearance. To test a vulnerability, measure the route's flow and then ask what happens when a defined function is disrupted.**

semanticAssessment.explanation: Amount, carrier turnover, selected cargo delivery and completed degradation differ. The A/B fictional interpretation is conditional: little additional LC3-II could reflect low formation, inadequate blockade, saturation or timing, not a uniquely diagnosed late blockage. evidence.supportingExcerpt: More lipidated LC3-II can reflect greater formation or slower removal. A controlled short lysosomal block and complementary tandem fluorescent LC3 reporter can help examine turnover and delivery to acidic compartments. Equal starting amounts can have different later fates. Little additional accumulation can reflect a late block, low formation or an unsuitable window; it does not establish dependence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Flux, selected-cargo clearance and survival dependence are different claims. NBR1 experiments identify selective ubiquitinated-cargo handling, not a universal LC3 cargo census. Use time courses, viable-cell normalisation, verified lysosomal inhibition and independent perturbations; autophagy proteins can have other functions. Lower mTOR signalling can change initiation without guaranteeing completed degradation. Typical research outputs include normalised LC3-II band intensity, reporter compartments per cell and selected-cargo disappearance over time. Tested cultures are consumed or perturbed, and prolonged lysosomal inhibition can itself disturb the system. No universal LC3 or flux cutoff selects treatment.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional one-hour recycling-station comparison starts with 20 waiting bags in each station. A receives 30 and processes 30, leaving 20; B receives five and processes none, leaving 25. Equal initial piles, including a six-bag schematic snapshot, cannot identify the rate or the later outcome. Bags are not LC3 molecules or assay thresholds: real markers are produced and removed, cargos differ, and a perturbation can affect several steps. Measure completion over time with appropriate controls. Even verified flow does not establish survival dependence; after a specific perturbation, more death can support a protective role, less drug-induced death can support a contribution to that death response, and changed flow with similar survival leaves timing or compensation as possible limits.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Macroautophagy encloses cargo in a double-membrane autophagosome, delivers it through lysosomal fusion and degrades it for reuse. Formation, delivery and breakdown are separate steps; not all lysosomal processes use autophagosomes. Active recycling often supports stress adaptation, whereas autophagy-dependent death requires causal evidence implicating the machinery.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Proteasomal degradation commonly handles individual suitable proteins, whereas lysosomal macroautophagy can deliver aggregates, organelles and portions of cytoplasm. This is a distinction of machinery and typical cargo, not an absolute partition: ubiquitinated material can also be recognised by autophagy adaptors such as p62. A tagged protein, an autophagic membrane marker and disappearance of a named cargo are different observations. Bortezomib's relapsed-myeloma trial result does not predict a hydroxychloroquine result in pancreatic cancer, and blocking both routes does not by itself demonstrate selective harm to malignant cells.

semanticAssessment.explanation: Direct target interaction, downstream flux and survival are separate measurements. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Bulk RNA abundance measures messages across the sampled cell mixture; it does not time cargo flow or establish dependence. ATG13 and the RB1CC1-encoded protein FIP200 participate with ULK1 in initiation machinery, as Ganley 2009 studied, but an alteration in a component does not establish the direction of completed recycling. A mechanistic dependence test should measure the proposed change before extensive death alters the markers, combine complementary readouts, and where feasible perturb more than one autophagy gene at different steps. Restoration and independent perturbations strengthen a specific causal explanation without making every genetic manipulation perfectly selective. A lower ATP or metabolic signal alone is neither counted death nor proof of autophagy dependence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

proofs.requirement: The next experiment targets a defined recycling function in culture A. It verifies that flux changes and measures survival. semanticAssessment.explanation: Direct target interaction, downstream flux and survival are separate measurements. Restoration and independent perturbations strengthen attribution with their own controls. A nonmalignant comparison is not automatically a validated normal-tissue model, and broad lysosomal effects do not establish route specificity or patient benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Bulk RNA abundance measures messages across the sampled cell mixture; it does not time cargo flow or establish dependence. ATG13 and the RB1CC1-encoded protein FIP200 participate with ULK1 in initiation machinery, as Ganley 2009 studied, but an alteration in a component does not establish the direction of completed recycling. A mechanistic dependence test should measure the proposed change before extensive death alters the markers, combine complementary readouts, and where feasible perturb more than one autophagy gene at different steps. Klionsky's guidelines also caution that these proteins have other functions. Restoration and independent perturbations strengthen a specific causal explanation without making every genetic manipulation perfectly selective. A lower ATP or metabolic signal alone is neither counted death nor proof of autophagy dependence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Target engagement is the separate question of whether a compound interacts with its target where the experiment needs it. The cellular thermal shift assay, introduced by Martinez Molina and colleagues, is built on ligand-induced thermal stabilisation of target proteins and was used to monitor drug binding in cells and tissue samples; a shift can support engagement under the assay conditions and is not by itself an inhibition or occupancy percentage. Engagement, a change in target function and cell survival are three measurements, and an effect on viability does not identify the responsible target.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Proteasomal degradation commonly handles individual suitable proteins, whereas lysosomal macroautophagy can deliver aggregates, organelles and portions of cytoplasm. This is a distinction of machinery and typical cargo, not an absolute partition: ubiquitinated material can also be recognised by autophagy adaptors such as p62. A tagged protein, an autophagic membrane marker and disappearance of a named cargo are different observations. Bortezomib's relapsed-myeloma trial result does not predict a hydroxychloroquine result in pancreatic cancer, and blocking both routes does not by itself demonstrate selective harm to malignant cells.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. evidence.supportingExcerpt: Lipid metabolism includes synthesis, uptake, storage, membrane remodelling and oxidation. evidence.supportingExcerpt: The branch experiments further narrowed an invasive-morphology question in MDA-MB-231. Blocking the geranylgeranylation branch had a larger effect than the tested sterol-branch block, and GGPP partly restored invasive growth after mutant-p53 depletion or statin treatment. In a fictional supply comparison, synthesis falls under an inhibitor in both lipid-poor and lipid-rich medium, but growth slows mainly in the former while import is stipulated to compensate in the latter. proofs.heading: A rescue experiment needs a precise question
proofs.requirement: A **rescue** supplies or restores something expected to reverse the proposed effect. It can strengthen a causal explanation, but what it supplies matters. Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase in the mevalonate pathway. That pathway supplies cholesterol and other products. Restoring mevalonate can rescue several downstream functions, so it does not uniquely prove cholesterol depletion caused the outcome.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: A **rescue** supplies or restores something expected to reverse the proposed effect. It can strengthen a causal explanation, but what it supplies matters. Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase in the mevalonate pathway. That pathway supplies cholesterol and other products. Restoring mevalonate can rescue several downstream functions, so it does not uniquely prove cholesterol depletion caused the outcome.

semanticAssessment.explanation: Mevalonate restores several branches. Controlled branch perturbations, selective add-backs and direct metabolite measurements can narrow causality; the rescue alone does not identify cholesterol or clinical exposure.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase upstream in the mevalonate pathway, which supplies cholesterol and nonsterol products. In Freed-Pastor and colleagues' breast-cancer 3D cultures, geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate partially rescued an invasive phenotype after mutant-p53 depletion or simvastatin treatment. This illustrates why mevalonate rescue alone cannot uniquely attribute an effect to cholesterol. It does not identify every relevant metabolite, establish a universal cancer dependency or show that a statin perturbation reproduces every change in SCAP-SREBP regulation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: HMG-CoA reductase makes mevalonate and is inhibited by statins. The downstream pathway branches: farnesyl pyrophosphate, FPP, feeds sterol synthesis through squalene and GGPP production as well as supplying protein prenylation; geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate, GGPP, supplies another prenylation route. Farnesyl and geranylgeranyl lipid modifications help position specified RAS- and RHO-family proteins, respectively. Cholesterol is a membrane component and a precursor of steroid hormones. Cholesterol amount, sterol synthesis and the whole mevalonate pathway are therefore different measurements. SCAP-SREBP sterol sensing regulates synthesis and uptake, but its activity, pathway transcripts, metabolite supply and dependence must each be established in the tested cells and medium.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A variant of uncertain significance (VUS) is a genetic change that has been detected but whose effect on disease is not yet known. Such findings are common on germline panels and in tumour sequencing, and they should not drive treatment decisions; over time many are reclassified through ClinVar, functional assays and population data. The term is linked to the Germline (hereditary) testing and Comprehensive genomic profiling technologies, to the ClinVar collection and AlphaMissense, and to the terms Mutation, Genomic profiling and Hereditary cancer syndromes. It appears in the bottleneck on unidentified inherited risk, and ideas that respond to it include testing every possible mutation in every cancer gene so no result is uncertain, and a plain-language version of every genomic report.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: A compound lowers lipid synthesis. Adding mevalonate restores growth. May the researcher conclude that the cells died specifically because cholesterol was missing?

semanticAssessment.explanation: Mevalonate restores several branches. Controlled branch perturbations, selective add-backs and direct metabolite measurements can narrow causality; the rescue alone does not identify cholesterol or clinical exposure.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase upstream in the mevalonate pathway, which supplies cholesterol and nonsterol products. In Freed-Pastor and colleagues' breast-cancer 3D cultures, geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate partially rescued an invasive phenotype after mutant-p53 depletion or simvastatin treatment. This illustrates why mevalonate rescue alone cannot uniquely attribute an effect to cholesterol. It does not identify every relevant metabolite, establish a universal cancer dependency or show that a statin perturbation reproduces every change in SCAP-SREBP regulation.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: HMG-CoA reductase makes mevalonate and is inhibited by statins. The downstream pathway branches: farnesyl pyrophosphate, FPP, feeds sterol synthesis through squalene and GGPP production as well as supplying protein prenylation; geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate, GGPP, supplies another prenylation route. Farnesyl and geranylgeranyl lipid modifications help position specified RAS- and RHO-family proteins, respectively. Cholesterol is a membrane component and a precursor of steroid hormones. Cholesterol amount, sterol synthesis and the whole mevalonate pathway are therefore different measurements. SCAP-SREBP sterol sensing regulates synthesis and uptake, but its activity, pathway transcripts, metabolite supply and dependence must each be established in the tested cells and medium.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Common contact-dependent Notch signaling begins when Delta-like or Jagged ligand on one cell engages a receptor on a neighbor. Ligand-regulated extracellular cleavage permits subsequent gamma-secretase-mediated membrane cleavage; the released Notch intracellular domain, NICD, can enter the nucleus and work with transcriptional partners. This route differs from an RTK phosphorylation relay and omits receptor maturation and sender mechanics.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A fictional T-ALL culture with high nuclear NICD without a ligand-bearing neighbor, and lower NICD after gamma-secretase blockade, supports a ligand-independent activation hypothesis. A contact-blocking experiment that lowers NICD without changing growth instead supports reduced received signaling without demonstrating a growth requirement. Control general toxicity, contact conditions, independent pathway perturbations and compensation. Gamma-secretase also processes other proteins; responsive HES/HEY RNA and nuclear staining need validated assays and are not universal eligibility cutoffs.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The original FIGHT-202 report observed responses in 38 of 107 people, 35.5 per cent, with previously treated cholangiocarcinoma and qualifying FGFR2 fusions or rearrangements given pemigatinib. The denominator includes fusions or rearrangements, not only one fusion mechanism. A 2024 correction is linked to the report; its text was unavailable, so the figure here is from the original abstract rather than a correction-checked final estimate. It is a named single-arm clinical signal rather than evidence for any receptor variant or another disease. For an uncharacterised receptor variant, compare with the normal receptor at matched expression and measure appropriate phosphorylation and downstream changes. Similar amount without extra activation does not support activation in that condition, while leaving other conditions unresolved. An activating receptor fusion or amplification may still require its kinase, whereas an active downstream RAS route can bypass the proposed receptor step. Locate the drug's blocked step and possible downstream bypass, then separately test whether changing the output matters for growth. Neither a bulk ligand signal from a sender nor receptor presence assigns an active signal to the malignant receiver.

proofs.requirement:

sourceRefs.exactPassage:
| Circuit | Locate the active step | A tempting overread |

semanticAssessment.explanation: Total beta-catenin includes adhesion; nuclear output, secreted-ligand dependence and growth are different. The two fictional cultures have a stipulated downstream bypass, while WNT974 is separate phase-1 human evidence rather than their response forecast.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Canonical pathway output, dependence on secreted Wnt, growth dependence and clinical response are separate claims. Nuclear beta-catenin can reflect pathway signaling, whereas total beta-catenin also includes adhesion functions. Lower AXIN2 RNA supports an output effect with suitable controls, not selective killing or patient benefit. Wnt routes that do not use beta-catenin are outside this canonical readout.

Canonical Wnt uses Frizzled with LRP5/6 co-receptor machinery. Without an effective signal, the Axin/APC-organized destruction machinery and sequential kinase steps promote beta-catenin degradation; signaling can change that control and allow nuclear regulation with partners. PORCN supplies a lipid modification required for proper Wnt secretion in the studied systems. Blocking that upstream step need not overcome a downstream escape from destruction control.

Two fictional cultures have nuclear beta-catenin. Secretion blockade reduces the nuclear signal in culture A but not in culture B, where downstream bypass is stipulated. A supports a ligand-dependent hypothesis; B illustrates how an upstream block can leave a downstream output intact. The symbols represent qualitative readouts, not protein counts or a real drug dataset. Neither pattern alone establishes selective killing; measure viability and control intervention specificity.

Assays can measure localization, AXIN2 RNA or a defined transcriptional reporter, before and after a specified perturbation. Preservation, composition, global transcription effects, model validation and tissue consumption matter; there is no universal Wnt-high treatment cutoff. In Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study of 94 people with advanced solid tumors, AXIN2 fell in many paired biopsies while no RECIST responses were observed. Target-related output and tumor response must therefore be reported separately, alongside safety rather than a claim of demonstrated benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Jiang 2013 screened 39 pancreatic cancer lines: the lines sensitive to the tested PORCN inhibitor carried inactivating RNF43 changes. This does not mean every RNF43 variant predicts sensitivity. The reported RNF43-loss models depended on secreted Wnt, whereas a downstream escape from beta-catenin destruction can maintain output despite blocking ligand preparation upstream. Morin's colorectal work linked stabilising beta-catenin changes to this distinction. In a fictional nuclear-beta-catenin culture with such a bypass stipulated, an upstream PORCN block is not expected to remove that particular output. Actual engagement, output and growth still need testing; pathway position is a mechanistic hypothesis, not proof that a drug has no effect through any route.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study treated 94 people with advanced solid tumours. AXIN2 RNA decreased in 94 per cent of 52 paired skin-biopsy comparisons and 74 per cent of 35 paired tumour-biopsy comparisons; no RECIST responses were observed. These denominators are paired-sample groups, not response fractions out of all 94 participants. A downstream output change supports a pharmacodynamic effect without directly measuring receptor occupancy, selective growth dependence or tumour shrinkage. Dysgeusia occurred in 50 per cent, illustrating that normal-tissue effects also matter. This trial does not justify transferring a target-output change to benefit or a treatment recommendation.

proofs.heading: Worked example: three fictional experiment cards
proofs.requirement: **Card B: two Wnt cultures.** Both show nuclear β-catenin and a responsive transcript. semanticAssessment.explanation: Total beta-catenin includes adhesion; nuclear output, secreted-ligand dependence and growth are different. The two fictional cultures have a stipulated downstream bypass, while WNT974 is separate phase-1 human evidence rather than their response forecast.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Canonical pathway output, dependence on secreted Wnt, growth dependence and clinical response are separate claims. Nuclear beta-catenin can reflect pathway signaling, whereas total beta-catenin also includes adhesion functions. Lower AXIN2 RNA supports an output effect with suitable controls, not selective killing or patient benefit. Wnt routes that do not use beta-catenin are outside this canonical readout.

Canonical Wnt uses Frizzled with LRP5/6 co-receptor machinery. Without an effective signal, the Axin/APC-organized destruction machinery and sequential kinase steps promote beta-catenin degradation; signaling can change that control and allow nuclear regulation with partners. PORCN supplies a lipid modification required for proper Wnt secretion in the studied systems. Blocking that upstream step need not overcome a downstream escape from destruction control.

Two fictional cultures have nuclear beta-catenin. Secretion blockade reduces the nuclear signal in culture A but not in culture B, where downstream bypass is stipulated. A supports a ligand-dependent hypothesis; B illustrates how an upstream block can leave a downstream output intact. The symbols represent qualitative readouts, not protein counts or a real drug dataset. Neither pattern alone establishes selective killing; measure viability and control intervention specificity.

Assays can measure localization, AXIN2 RNA or a defined transcriptional reporter, before and after a specified perturbation. Preservation, composition, global transcription effects, model validation and tissue consumption matter; there is no universal Wnt-high treatment cutoff. In Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study of 94 people with advanced solid tumors, AXIN2 fell in many paired biopsies while no RECIST responses were observed. Target-related output and tumor response must therefore be reported separately, alongside safety rather than a claim of demonstrated benefit.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Jiang 2013 screened 39 pancreatic cancer lines: the lines sensitive to the tested PORCN inhibitor carried inactivating RNF43 changes. This does not mean every RNF43 variant predicts sensitivity. The reported RNF43-loss models depended on secreted Wnt, whereas a downstream escape from beta-catenin destruction can maintain output despite blocking ligand preparation upstream. Morin's colorectal work linked stabilising beta-catenin changes to this distinction. In a fictional nuclear-beta-catenin culture with such a bypass stipulated, an upstream PORCN block is not expected to remove that particular output. Actual engagement, output and growth still need testing; pathway position is a mechanistic hypothesis, not proof that a drug has no effect through any route.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study treated 94 people with advanced solid tumours. AXIN2 RNA decreased in 94 per cent of 52 paired skin-biopsy comparisons and 74 per cent of 35 paired tumour-biopsy comparisons; no RECIST responses were observed. These denominators are paired-sample groups, not response fractions out of all 94 participants. A downstream output change supports a pharmacodynamic effect without directly measuring receptor occupancy, selective growth dependence or tumour shrinkage. Dysgeusia occurred in 50 per cent, illustrating that normal-tissue effects also matter. This trial does not justify transferring a target-output change to benefit or a treatment recommendation.

evidence.supportingExcerpt:
Canonical pathway output, dependence on secreted Wnt, growth dependence and clinical response are separate claims. Nuclear beta-catenin can reflect pathway signaling, whereas total beta-catenin also includes adhesion functions. Lower AXIN2 RNA supports an output effect with suitable controls, not selective killing or patient benefit. Wnt routes that do not use beta-catenin are outside this canonical readout.

Canonical Wnt uses Frizzled with LRP5/6 co-receptor machinery. Without an effective signal, the Axin/APC-organized destruction machinery and sequential kinase steps promote beta-catenin degradation; signaling can change that control and allow nuclear regulation with partners. PORCN supplies a lipid modification required for proper Wnt secretion in the studied systems. Blocking that upstream step need not overcome a downstream escape from destruction control.

Two fictional cultures have nuclear beta-catenin. Secretion blockade reduces the nuclear signal in culture A but not in culture B, where downstream bypass is stipulated. A supports a ligand-dependent hypothesis; B illustrates how an upstream block can leave a downstream output intact. The symbols represent qualitative readouts, not protein counts or a real drug dataset. Neither pattern alone establishes selective killing; measure viability and control intervention specificity.

Assays can measure localization, AXIN2 RNA or a defined transcriptional reporter, before and after a specified perturbation. proofs.heading: What can go wrong at this step
proofs.requirement: Three shortcuts are especially tempting: turning a CUL3 variant into assumed NRF2 activation; turning antioxidant amount into ferroptosis sensitivity; and turning a BET-family alteration into response to any BET inhibitor.

sourceRefs.exactPassage: Three shortcuts are especially tempting: turning a CUL3 variant into assumed NRF2 activation; turning antioxidant amount into ferroptosis sensitivity; and turning a BET-family alteration into response to any BET inhibitor.

semanticAssessment.explanation: No causal chain is supplied by a gene-family name, antioxidant RNA, probe-associated death or the addition of two hypotheses. Specificity, mechanism, exposure and clinical evidence remain distinct.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Protection and dependence are experiment-specific directions. If removing a verified defence makes a defined stress more lethal, that supports protection under that stress. If removing the defence or a supply route reduces survival relative to an appropriate matched comparison, that supports a conditional dependence; it need not mean every unstressed cell dies. In a fictional culture, high antioxidant RNA plus probe-associated death establishes neither NRF2-driven killing nor ferroptosis. Test the alteration's effect on NRF2 turnover or nuclear localisation and output, then use independent perturbation and restoration to examine the survival mechanism. CUL3 works with other adaptors, and a compound suppressing protein production broadly does not isolate NRF2. A genetic intervention also needs controls, rather than being automatically specific.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Vartanian and colleagues examined brusatol in the KEAP1-mutant lung-cancer line A549. Protein profiling and measurements of newly synthesised proteins supported broad inhibition of protein synthesis, with NRF2 falling among many proteins. Cytotoxicity across additional cancer cell lines was not restricted to KEAP1-NRF2 activity. A lower NRF2 signal after this compound therefore does not isolate NRF2 inhibition as the cause of death. Check general translation early and use independently controlled perturbations before attributing a survival effect to the proposed defence.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Assigning ferroptosis needs convergent measurements of death, lipid damage preceding death, iron dependence and appropriately controlled rescue. Independent genetic and chemical perturbations strengthen attribution; rescue alone is not complete proof. Probe chemistry, concentration, nutrients, cell density and observation time can alter results. A lipid-probe ratio and death fraction are different outputs, with no universal diagnostic staining threshold. Live death and rescue tests consume viable model material. Specify lipid-probe oxidation ratios and independently measured death percentages over a stated interval; a marker snapshot does not reconstruct the full causal sequence.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Extracellular flux methods estimate respiratory and glycolytic contributions to energy production under defined assumptions. A respiratory message, measured oxygen use, calculated energy output and dependence for survival are distinct claims. Normalisation, fuel, viable-cell input, collection time and the specified method version belong with a result. Electron transport, proton pumping, return through ATP synthase and uncoupling are distinct steps. The mitochondrial matrix and intermembrane space locate the two sides of the inner membrane; naming these compartments does not supply a universal conversion ratio.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Respiration and ATP generation are related but different measurements. Respiratory transcripts, normalised oxygen-consumption rates and survival dependence cannot substitute for one another; bulk tissue composition and compensatory fuel use also matter. Oxygen-consumption assays require viable cells or functional preparations rather than routine fixed sections and use or perturb the tested material. evidence.supportingExcerpt: An oxidation-sensitive fluorescence signal needs a named probe, loading and cell-health controls, location, timing and appropriate calibration. HyPer and HyPer7 are peroxide reporters with distinct pH and sensitivity properties, rather than universal measurements of all reactive oxygen species. Fixed-tissue damage staining cannot reconstruct a live chemical rate. Live reporters require viable material or engineered models. Outputs can be relative fluorescence or calibrated ratios; unstimulated, positive, probe-only and cell-health controls address different failure modes. evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Protection and dependence are experiment-specific directions. If removing a verified defence makes a defined stress more lethal, that supports protection under that stress. If removing the defence or a supply route reduces survival relative to an appropriate matched comparison, that supports a conditional dependence; it need not mean every unstressed cell dies. In a fictional culture, high antioxidant RNA plus probe-associated death establishes neither NRF2-driven killing nor ferroptosis. Test the alteration's effect on NRF2 turnover or nuclear localisation and output, then use independent perturbation and restoration to examine the survival mechanism. CUL3 works with other adaptors, and a compound suppressing protein production broadly does not isolate NRF2. A genetic intervention also needs controls, rather than being automatically specific.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Assigning ferroptosis needs convergent measurements of death, lipid damage preceding death, iron dependence and appropriately controlled rescue. proofs.requirement: A metabolic program is easier to read when you name the process it describes:

sourceRefs.exactPassage: A metabolic program is easier to read when you name the process it describes:

semanticAssessment.explanation: Aerobic lactate production can coexist with respiration and does not diagnose hypoxia. AMPK and UPR outputs can accompany adaptation; hypoxia-response RNA is not an exact oxygen concentration.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The Warburg effect describes substantial glucose-to-lactate metabolism with oxygen available. Glycolysis can supply ATP and lactate formation regenerates a carrier needed for its continuation. Lactate production does not imply absent mitochondrial oxidation, and proliferating normal cells can use aerobic glycolysis too.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Lactate release, oxygen consumption and labelled glucose reaching mitochondrial metabolites can coexist. High pathway activity, a transcript signature or glucose uptake does not prove survival dependence. A culture nutrient-removal experiment does not establish that changing a person's diet selectively starves a tumour or identifies a medicine. Functional rate or tracer studies use viable cells, slices or a defined in-vivo experiment and consume or perturb material. No universal Warburg-positive threshold predicts treatment benefit; a functional perturbation and survival outcome are separate from the metabolic pattern.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: LKB1 and a calcium-sensitive CaMKK2 route can activate AMPK in suitable systems. AMPK can phosphorylate raptor and restrain mTORC1, connecting energy supply to costly growth-related work. An AMPK phosphosite does not uniquely identify glucose deprivation or every nutrient signal.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: During energy stress in model experiments, AMPK preserved reducing power through altered fatty-acid metabolism and supported survival. Increased AMPK and raptor phosphorylation, slower growth and greater survival than an AMPK-deficient comparison are compatible observations. This is not a universal benefit from activating or inhibiting AMPK.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: ER stress is an imbalance between protein-folding demand and local capacity; the unfolded protein response is an adaptation programme, not the same thing as the stress. IRE1 processes XBP1 RNA, PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and ATF6 processing releases a nuclear regulator. Distinct branches can alter folding capacity, incoming translation and disposal.
evidence.sourceReadingBoundary: Only the assigned scientific or inferential claim is accepted at its recorded source depth; an exact field quotation does not re-certify every older claim in that field.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Specify preserved material, RNA quality, isoform-specific methods, total-protein controls, timing and identified cell populations. semanticAssessment.explanation: Stable viable counts with lower ATP-associated signal do not establish cell killing. Regrowth concerns survivors, while probe chemistry and compartment validation are needed before assigning a reactive species or mitochondrial origin.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Yap 2023 reported phase 1 IACS-010759 studies in 17 people with acute myeloid leukaemia and 23 with advanced solid tumours. Elevated blood lactate and neurotoxicity limited exposure needed for sustained complex-I inhibition; target inhibition was modest, antitumour activity limited, no recommended phase 2 dose was established and both studies were discontinued. These named safety and exposure results separate a model vulnerability from a usable treatment. A respiratory RNA signature plus a lower ATP-based signal still establishes neither increased oxygen-consumption rate nor counted cell death. Measure identified viable cells, normalised oxygen use, engagement and independent growth or death outcomes. Acidification can include respiratory carbon dioxide as well as glycolysis, and lactate production with oxygen can coexist with respiration.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: An oxidation-sensitive fluorescence signal needs a named probe, loading and cell-health controls, location, timing and appropriate calibration. HyPer and HyPer7 are peroxide reporters with distinct pH and sensitivity properties, rather than universal measurements of all reactive oxygen species. Fixed-tissue damage staining cannot reconstruct a live chemical rate. Live reporters require viable material or engineered models. Outputs can be relative fluorescence or calibrated ratios; unstimulated, positive, probe-only and cell-health controls address different failure modes. The result is not a universal concentration of all reactive oxygen species.

proofs.heading: Test the proposed consequence
proofs.requirement: If the claim is energy dependence, follow ATP supply, compensatory pathways and survival. If it is lipid-driven death, follow lipid oxidation, iron dependence and suitable rescue. Do not use one kind of rescue to answer every question.

semanticAssessment.explanation: Energy dependence requires ATP supply, compensation and controlled survival measurements; ferroptosis instead requires convergent iron-dependent lipid damage and rescue. A general antioxidant does not answer every mechanism or safety question.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Respiration and ATP generation are related but different measurements. Mitochondrial and nonmitochondrial oxygen consumption, proton leak and ATP-linked respiration require controlled separation. Respiratory transcripts, normalised oxygen-consumption rates and survival dependence cannot substitute for one another; bulk tissue composition and compensatory fuel use also matter. Oxygen-consumption assays require viable cells or functional preparations rather than routine fixed sections and use or perturb the tested material. Report oxygen per time with justified viable-cell or protein normalisation. Equal baseline respiration and different responses to ATP-synthase inhibition do not by themselves identify which culture will die.

semanticAssessment.explanation: Composition, cell number, fuel, oxygen, density and timing can explain differences. Respiratory CO2 contributes to acidification, RNA ranks are not calibrated dependence, and high messages plus a lower ATP signal show neither high flux nor selective death.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Respiration and ATP generation are related but different measurements. Mitochondrial and nonmitochondrial oxygen consumption, proton leak and ATP-linked respiration require controlled separation. Respiratory transcripts, normalised oxygen-consumption rates and survival dependence cannot substitute for one another; bulk tissue composition and compensatory fuel use also matter. Oxygen-consumption assays require viable cells or functional preparations rather than routine fixed sections and use or perturb the tested material. Report oxygen per time with justified viable-cell or protein normalisation. Equal baseline respiration and different responses to ATP-synthase inhibition do not by themselves identify which culture will die.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Extracellular acidification can include respiration-derived carbon dioxide as well as glycolytic acid production. Keep correction assumptions, normalisation and method version with any calculated ATP rate. The 2018 correction to Mookerjee and colleagues' 2017 method changes the ATP-linked oxygen-rate equation and reports use of a different hyperpolarization factor in some calculations; several numerical rates changed while the authors retained their qualitative conclusions. An inhibitor-sensitive oxygen-rate difference is therefore not itself an ATP rate, and an unversioned fixed conversion should not be inferred.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional paired-well example, culture A uses 180 picomoles of oxygen per minute with 30,000 viable cells and B uses 120 with 20,000. Both equal 60 per minute per 10,000 viable cells. After ATP-synthase blockade their corresponding normalised rates are 30 and 40, giving inhibitor-sensitive differences of 30 and 20 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 cells. Those are oxygen-rate differences, not ATP-production rates or proof of survival dependence. Cell number, fuel, oxygen, timing and the inhibitor controls matter. A corrected, specified conversion method needs additional assumptions; the 2018 Mookerjee correction changed calculations by up to 17 per cent. General oxidation, compartment-specific reactive chemistry and iron-dependent lipid death remain separate questions.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: Yap 2023 reported phase 1 IACS-010759 studies in 17 people with acute myeloid leukaemia and 23 with advanced solid tumours. Elevated blood lactate and neurotoxicity limited exposure needed for sustained complex-I inhibition; target inhibition was modest, antitumour activity limited, no recommended phase 2 dose was established and both studies were discontinued. These named safety and exposure results separate a model vulnerability from a usable treatment. A respiratory RNA signature plus a lower ATP-based signal still establishes neither increased oxygen-consumption rate nor counted cell death. Measure identified viable cells, normalised oxygen use, engagement and independent growth or death outcomes. Acidification can include respiratory carbon dioxide as well as glycolysis, and lactate production with oxygen can coexist with respiration.
